title: Cryopreservation of mammalian cells
summary: Freeze cells safely in liquid-nitrogen storage with controlled-rate cooling.

reagents.name: Freezing medium (90% FBS + 10% DMSO, or commercial)

hazardsMd: Liquid N2 burns and asphyxiation hazard. Always wear face shield + cryo gloves. Vials can explode if liquid N2 leaks in; transfer to vapor phase only.
contentUndergrad:
## Why DMSO
DMSO penetrates cells and prevents intracellular ice crystals during freezing. The trade-off: it's toxic at room temperature, so freeze fast and thaw faster.

steps.title: Trypsinize cells (per cell-culture-passage)
steps.instructionMd: Reach a single-cell suspension following the standard passage protocol.
steps.verificationMd: Suspension uniform, no clumps under microscope.

steps.title: Count and pellet
steps.instructionMd: Count cells (hemocytometer or automated). Spin 200×g / 5 min. Aspirate supernatant.
steps.verificationMd: Visible pellet at the tube bottom. Supernatant fully removed (no residual liquid).

steps.title: Resuspend in freezing medium
steps.instructionMd: Resuspend pellet at 1-5×10^6 cells/mL in cold freezing medium. Aliquot 1 mL per cryovial. Label vials with line, passage, date, your initials.
steps.safetyNotesMd: Work fast — DMSO is toxic at room temp.
steps.verificationMd: All vials labeled. Volumes consistent (~1 mL each).

steps.title: Controlled-rate freeze
steps.instructionMd: Place vials in a Mr Frosty (or equivalent) at −80 °C overnight. Achieves ~1 °C/min cooling.
steps.verificationMd: Mr Frosty's isopropanol level adequate. Vials seated upright.

steps.title: Transfer to liquid N2
steps.instructionMd: Within 24 hours, transfer vials to liquid-nitrogen storage (vapor phase, never liquid phase for biohazard vials). Update the freezer inventory.
steps.safetyNotesMd: Wear face shield + cryo gloves. Long pants, closed-toe shoes mandatory.
steps.verificationMd: Vials in their assigned rack/box position. Inventory log updated with date, contents, location.
